chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Hamzah ibn Bazee' from Ali al-Sa'i who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, I used to practice Mut'ah (temporary marriage), but I disliked it and took it as an ill omen, so I gave Allah a pledge between the Rukn and the Maqam, and made upon myself a vow and fasting that I would not marry it. Then that became difficult for me, and I regretted my oath, and I did not have the means in my hand to marry it publicly.' He said, 'You made a covenant with Allah that you would not obey Him, and by Allah, if you do not obey Him, you will disobey Him.'

key_terms.اَلرُّكْن: The Rukn (a corner of the Kaaba)
key_terms.اَلْمَقَام: The Maqam (Station of Abraham near the Kaaba)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on breaking a vow to abstain from a permissible act like temporary marriage?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal status of a vow to abstain from a permissible act (Mut'ah), noting that the vow itself creates an obligation to maintain the abstention. The Imam’s statement, 'If you do not obey Him [by keeping the vow], you will disobey Him,' highlights the principle that fulfilling the vow is an act of obedience, while breaking it without valid excuse constitutes disobedience to the vow's binding nature. This reflects the Shia juristic view that vows regarding permissible acts are binding unless a specific condition for release is met, emphasizing the seriousness of one's word before Allah.
